# Tripo 2.5: Multiview to Model

Two photos of one object — a front and a back — become a single textured 3D model. Tripo takes the
silhouette and the surface detail from the front view, uses the back view for what the front cannot
see, and returns a GLB plus an FBX that drop straight into a scene, a game engine or a render.

Pinned to **`v2.5-20250123`**. The node also lists v3.0 and v3.1; those engines bill differently and
ship as their own templates (`Tripo3.0: Multiview to Model`, `Tripo H3.1: Multiview to Model`), so
switch `model_version` only to compare quality, not to save credits.

| Front view — `image` (required) | Back view — `image_back` (optional) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Front view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/api_tripo_multiview_to_model_front_image.jpg) | ![Back view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/api_tripo_multiview_to_model_back_image.jpg) |

- `image` — the front. The only required slot; the whole model is built around it.
- `image_back` — the far side: back plates, hair, a tail, folded wings. Leave it empty and Tripo
  invents the unseen half, which is fine for a simple shape and wrong for anything with a back story.
- `image_left` / `image_right` — side views, unused here. Worth filling in when the design is
  profile-heavy (boots, snouts, fins).
- One object per image, same scale, plain background, no cast shadows. Mismatched scale comes back
  as a squashed or stretched mesh, and no later step repairs it.

## The Tripo toolset

Everything after the generation node sits in the *Tripo Toolset* group, bypassed: each step is a
separate Tripo call with its own charge, so enable only what the shot needs — select the nodes and
press `ctrl + B`.

| Node | What it does | Enable when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tripo: Multiview to Model** | Front + back → textured mesh (`model_version v2.5-20250123`, `face_limit -1`, standard geometry, `original_image` texture alignment) | always — this is the node the template runs |
| **Tripo: Rig** | Builds a skeleton; `rig_type auto` picks biped / quadruped / hexapod / octopod from the mesh | the model has to move or be posed |
| **Tripo: Retarget** | Plays a preset animation on a rig — `preset:idle` here, plus walk, run, jump, slash, shoot and the full `preset:biped:*` set | after Rig; needs a `rig task id`, not a model id |
| **Tripo: Convert** | Re-exports the task as GLTF / USDZ / FBX / OBJ / STL / 3MF, with quad output, face limit, texture size, pivot to centre-bottom, flatten bottom, pack UV and an FBX preset | a downstream tool needs another container or a poly budget |
| **Tripo: Smart UV** | Re-unwraps the UVs and bakes the existing textures onto the new layout; capped at 80,000 triangles | the texture has to be hand-painted or edited per island |
| **Tripo: Texture v2** | Regenerates the texture from a prompt or a style image, keeping the geometry | the shape is right and the surface is wrong |

Chaining: `Multiview to Model → (Rig) → (Retarget) → Smart UV / Texture v2 → Convert → Save`. Every
toolset node reads `model task_id` (or `rig task_id`) from the node above it — drop that wire and the
step has nothing to work on. `Smart UV` and `Texture v2` both hand back a new task id, so the
downstream node has to point at the newest one, not at the original generation task.

## Outputs

Two `Save 3D` nodes write into `3d/`: `3d/tripo_multiview_to_model` for the GLB and
`3d/tripo_multiview_to_model_fbx` for the FBX, both taken from the same generation task.
